body:
- I don't see why using `code` tags and explicitly ignoring the lint warning to refer to the existing methods and signals.
- The few times it's mentioned in the class reference, it's "causes infinite recursion".
- There's `CONNECT_DEFERRED` and `call_deferred()` which I would recommend heavily more for this purpose.
	- `await` is a GDScript-exclusive concept and, it's somewhat harder to follow the order of operations with it, especially in this case.
	- Or even `set_block_signals`? I think that, based on what is being described, it would actually prevent this.
```suggestion
		[b]Note:[/b] Several methods of this class, such as [method get_next_path_position], can trigger a new path calculation. Calling these from an agent's signal, such as [signal waypoint_reached], can cause infinite recursion. It is recommended to call these methods in the physics step, or delay their call until the end of the frame (see [method Object.call_deferred] or [constant Object.CONNECT_DEFERRED]).
```

body:
Do link them, by all means.

> I broke up the sentence into two short sentences to make it easier to read and comprehend (I'm always trying to improve on that front).
> If you feel like I managed to achieve that goal, I'd like to keep it.

It's a pretty good idea most of the times. This time though, I personally feel like the two sentences are so related to one another ("It is recommended to do *this* or *that*") that it breaks the flow a little. Especially because in one sentence the verb is in its infinite form ("to call") and in the other it's imperative, basically a command ("delay").

So to be consistent the sentences should be `Call these methods [...]. Alternatively, delay their call [...]`. By doing that you may notice how short these tips are in practice, hence my suggestion to merge them.
